page: Amazon Web Services i4g.2xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton2 processor using ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz, it allocates one physical core per vCPU without simultaneous multithreading. The hardware configuration features 64 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, paired with a bundled 1875 GB local NVMe SSD and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data reflects mid-tier throughput across multi-core and input/output workloads alongside modest single-thread compute capabilities. In stress-ng, the instance achieves average-tier scores of 1519.59 for single-core and 12132.09 for multi-core testing. Memory throughput benchmarks show read bandwidth of 116.33 GB/s and write bandwidth of 55.8 GB/s on large uncached blocks. In application-focused metrics, it sustained 9.8 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 9.71 GB/s in static web serving throughput, and an average-tier database operations score of 5224.61 in PassMark. However, integer compression, text processing, cryptographic tests, and LLM token generation demonstrate weak to poor relative performance due to lower single-thread execution ceilings and the absence of specialized x86 vector extensions.

From an infrastructure cost-efficiency perspective, the Graviton2 processor architecture yields favorable density and resource efficiency for high-IOPS transactional storage tasks when compared to legacy x86 storage instances. Tradeoffs center on the architecture requiring arm64 binary compatibility and the performance penalty on compute-heavy single-threaded tasks. The instance is suited for local NVMe caching tiers, transactional NoSQL systems like Redis or Cassandra, medium-scale relational databases, and log analysis engines.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance engineered around an 8-core AWS Graviton2 processor featuring ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores running at 2.5 GHz. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores, 64 GB of RAM, and a high-speed bundled 1875 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by a 5 Gbps baseline network link. Empirical benchmarks demonstrate solid mid-tier multi-threaded processing, achieving 9.8 million Redis SET operations per second and 5224.61 in PassMark database operations, although single-threaded execution and cryptographic calculations register in lower tiers. Balancing generous memory per core with direct NVMe storage bandwidth, the i4g.2xlarge delivers efficient resource density without the premium associated with traditional x86 storage instances. It is best suited for IOPS-sensitive workloads including NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, search indexing, and real-time analytics engines requiring fast local disk persistence.
